title: Khao Soi Chicken Curry Noodles with Crispy Noodle Topping
summary: A warming coconut curry noodle soup topped with tender braised chicken, crunchy fried noodles and fresh pickles for contrast.

ingredients.item: chicken stock, plus more if needed
fish sauce, plus more to taste

ingredients.note: about 60 g fried for the topping

ingredients.item: neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)
pickled mustard greens, rinsed and sliced

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large casserole over medium, add 40 g curry paste, 1 tsp curry powder and ½ tsp turmeric, and stir for 2-3 min until fragrant.

steps.title: Split
steps.text: Add 240 ml coconut milk and boil, stirring, until red oil separates, 3-4 min, then repeat with another 240 ml.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add the chicken legs, 360 ml stock and the last 240 ml coconut milk, bring back to the boil, then lower to a simmer with 1 tsp sugar and 2 tbsp fish sauce.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cover and simmer until the chicken is tender and reaches 74 °C at the bone, about 45 min, then taste and adjust so the curry is salty, spicy and a touch sweet.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Heat frying oil in a saucepan to about 180 °C, fry 60 g noodles in handfuls until crisp and golden, 1-2 min, and drain, then fry the dried chillies a few seconds until puffed and drain.

steps.title: Boil
steps.text: Cook the remaining noodles in plenty of water until just tender, 2-3 min, then drain.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Divide the noodles among bowls, add a chicken leg and plenty of curry, then top with shallots, pickled mustard greens, fried noodles, coriander and lime wedges, with the fried chillies on the side.

tips: Stir the curry paste constantly while it fries so the spices don't catch and turn bitter.
Taste the curry before serving; it should seem a touch too salty on its own, as the noodles and toppings will mellow it.
safety: Keep a close eye on the frying oil and never leave the pan unattended while crisping the noodles.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: The curry keeps covered in the fridge for a couple of days and reheats well on the hob, but fry the crispy noodle topping fresh just before serving. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
